groups.name: Chest
groups.desc: The pecs: the two big plates on the front of your ribcage. They push your arms forward and across your body, as in push-ups and presses.

groups.name: Back
groups.desc: Lats down the sides, traps across the top and middle, plus the small muscles on the shoulder blade and the spinal erectors low down. They pull your arms down and back and hold your spine upright.

groups.name: Front delts
groups.desc: The front of the shoulder cap. Lifts your arm forward and up. Every push-up and press works it, so it rarely needs its own exercise.

groups.name: Side delts
groups.desc: The outer cap of the shoulder, visible from both front and back. Lifts your arm out to the side and makes the shoulders look wider. Presses barely touch it; lateral raises are the main exercise.

groups.name: Rear delts
groups.desc: The back of the shoulder cap. Pulls your arm backward and out. Rows give it some work; rear-delt flys, face pulls and pull-aparts target it.

groups.name: Biceps
groups.desc: Front of the upper arm. Bends the elbow and turns the palm up. Rows and pulldowns help; curls target it.

groups.name: Triceps
groups.desc: Back of the upper arm, three heads. Straightens the elbow. Every press helps; overhead extensions reach the long head best.

groups.name: Quads
groups.desc: Front of the thigh, four muscles. Straightens the knee: squats, lunges, step-ups.

groups.name: Hamstrings
groups.desc: Back of the thigh. Bends the knee and extends the hip: Romanian deadlifts and leg curls.

groups.name: Glutes
groups.desc: The buttocks. Gluteus maximus extends the hip (bridges, squats); gluteus medius on the upper side steadies the pelvis on one leg.

groups.name: Calves
groups.desc: Back of the lower leg. The gastrocnemius (upper, two heads) works best with a straight knee; the soleus underneath works in any calf raise.

groups.name: Core
groups.desc: Abs down the front, obliques on the sides, and deep abs underneath that you can't see. They brace and bend the trunk.

groups.name: Rotator cuff
groups.desc: Four small muscles around the shoulder blade that hold the ball of the shoulder in its socket. Target about 3 sets a week: band external rotations, plus half credit from face pulls.

groups.name: Serratus
groups.desc: The finger-like muscle along your ribs under the armpit. It keeps your shoulder blades flat against your ribs. Target about 3 sets a week of push-up plus.

groups.name: Shins
groups.desc: Tibialis anterior, the muscle on the front of your shin. Lifts your toes; helps prevent shin splints and steadies your ankles. Target about 3 sets a week of wall tibialis raises.

exercises.name: Incline push-up
steps: Put your hands on a sturdy couch arm, counter or table edge, a bit wider than your shoulders.
Walk your feet back until your body is one straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest to the edge with elbows angled about 45° from your body.
Push back up until your arms are straight.
cues: The higher the surface, the easier it is. Lower it over the weeks.
Squeeze your glutes so your hips don't sag.

exercises.name: Push-up
steps: Start in a high plank, hands just wider than shoulders, body straight from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the floor, elbows about 45° from your sides.
Stop when your chest is a fist's height from the floor.
Press the floor away until your arms are straight.
cues: Knees down or hands on a couch if you can't get 6 good reps.
Keep your neck neutral; look at the floor just ahead of your hands.

exercises.name: Dumbbell floor press
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, a dumbbell in each hand resting on your chest.
Press the dumbbells straight up over your chest until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly until your upper arms touch the floor, then pause.
Press back up.
cues: The floor stops your elbows, which makes this shoulder-friendly.
